Subject: Kickoff: Dedicated GPU pool provisioning & regional failover plan

Hi team,

Quick handoff — NimbusAI agreed to move forward with Redwood Dedicated for production inference. Contract is signed (deal DL-2026-0987). They need a reserved GPU pool, autoscaling that supports predictable bursts for marketing campaigns, and a regional failover plan.

Primary asks from sales discovery:
- Initial steady-state throughput: ~200 concurrent inference RPS (avg 64-token completions)
- Peak bursts: expected up to ~450 RPS during campaigns (short windows)
- Latency SLO: 95th pct < 220ms token latency
- Data residency: EU/US customers, prefer EU primary if feasible

Monica — can you own the onboarding and run the kickoff with Dev for provisioning details? Dev, please prepare a recommended pool size, instance types, autoscale policy, and any network/VPC checks. Alex/Priya — sharing our kickoff cadence options: 30m tech review + 60m provisioning session.

Thanks — please reply with availability and any immediate blockers.

— Stephanie

On Thu, Aug 5, 2026 at 11:02 AM Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.inference.com> wrote:
> Dev — can you draft an initial GPU pool recommendation and autoscale/burst policy by EOD 08/05 so we can review in the tech kickoff?

Thanks — attached is a concise recommendation (high level below). I also uploaded the provisioning_template.xlsx pre-filled with the numbers we discussed.

Summary recommendation (initial deployment):
- Model profile: opensource-llm-large-v2 (decoder-only). Typical token length: 64 tokens; context up to 1024.
- GPU type: NVIDIA H100 (fp16 inference), chosen for throughput at 8k+ token lengths.
- Pool sizing: start with 8 GPUs (H100) in the primary region. This maps to ~200 sustained RPS at target batching (see batching notes).
- Autoscale policy: min_replicas=2, target_utilization=0.65, max_replicas=20.
- Burst allowance: enable burst pool up to +40% of max_replicas for short windows (30–90 minutes) with auto-rollback to baseline.
- Batching configuration: dynamic batching with preferred_batch_size=8, max_batch_latency_ms=15. Continuous KV cache enabled for conversational sessions to reduce token compute on warm prefixes.
- Cold-start mitigation: warmup containers during scheduled campaign windows; pre-warmed cache for top 20 prefixes.
- Regional failover: primary: us-west-2, failover: us-east-1 for lower-latency fallback within the US. If NimbusAI prefers EU primary, we can mirror config to eu-west-1 and replicate KV caches (see notes).

Networking & Ops notes (summary):
- VPC peering + static egress IPs recommended for allowlisting.
- Required ports and subnets listed in network_checklist.pdf.
- Provisioning lead time: 5 business days after we receive completed provisioning_template and network checklist + signed MOP (minor changes tolerated).

Attachments included in thread: provisioning_template.xlsx, network_checklist.pdf

If you want, I can turn the burst allowance into a hard quota controlled by an internal policy so we don't exceed cost expectations; that would require a quick sign-off on burst credits.

— Dev Patel
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Thanks for the detailed plan, Dev. A couple of clarifications from our side before the tech kickoff:

1) Region preference: NimbusAI actually needs EU primary (eu-west-1) to minimize latency for our EU customers. Can you mirror the same pool spec in eu-west-1 as primary and keep us-west-2 as failover?
2) Peak behaviour: when you say +40% burst up to max_replicas, are we able to cap burst spend separately from baseline reserved spend? We need to control excess spend during marketing spikes.
3) Procurement / contract question: what is the earliest date Redwood can guarantee reserved capacity billing starts? We may need the pool live by 2026-08-20.

We’ll bring finalized provisioning_template.xlsx and our network team to the 08/09 provisioning session.

Alex Morgan

Subject: Re: Kickoff: Dedicated GPU pool provisioning & regional failover plan

Alex — thanks, good catches. Summary of updates and actions based on your asks:

Decisions agreed:
- Primary region: eu-west-1 (mirror config). Failover: us-west-2.
- Pool size: 8 x H100 in eu-west-1 (initial); failover pool 4 x H100 in us-west-2 (warm standby).
- Autoscale: min_replicas=2, target_utilization=0.65, max_replicas=20 in primary. Burst: +40% capped by a burst-credit policy (you will see burst usage broken out in the console and we can cap at a dollar threshold).
- Billing: reserved capacity billing can be aligned to provision date. Earliest guaranteed billing start = 2026-08-18 if provisioning and MOP are signed by 08/12. If you need 08/17 start, we can expedite but will require DocuSign sign-off by EOD 08/10.

Action items:
- NimbusAI: complete provisioning_template.xlsx (attached) and network_checklist.pdf; confirm static egress IPs and provide contact for on-call network engineer (Priya, please share). Due: 08/10.
- Redwood (Dev): prepare a mirrored eu-west-1 template and cost estimate including burst-credit cap. Due: 08/09 (provisioning session).
- Redwood (Monica): schedule provisioning kickoff 08/09 09:00 PT (calendar invite sent).
- Finance/Sales (Stephanie): prepare updated order with 08/18 billing start contingency.

Links & attachments: provisioning_template.xlsx (filled by Redwood), network_checklist.pdf, DocuSign link for MOP: https://app.docusign.com/embeddedSigning/some-doc-id, HubSpot: https://hubspot.com/deal/DL-2026-0987

I’ll run the provisioning session notes and MOP checklist during the 08/09 meeting and capture sign-offs. If anyone needs to move dates tighter, flag it in this thread.

Best,
Monica Patel
